export const meta = {
  name: 'experiments-investigation-and-revision',
  description: 'Investigate Claude-experiment episodes, then revise style guide',
  phases: [{ title: 'Investigate' }, { title: 'Revise' }],
}

phase('Investigate')
const episodes = await agent(`Read-only analyst in /home/user/BookMinder (git repo, full history unshallowed). Modify nothing except your deliverable.

CONTEXT: The project author is separating THEIR intended BDD/TDD style from fallout of two experiments where Claude was given autonomy and the result was bad. Orientation: .coordination/process-evolution.md, repo-map.md, threads.md. Do NOT read claude-dev-log-diary/ contents.

INVESTIGATE TWO EPISODES chronologically, from git history (commits, diffs, messages, dates):

EPISODE A — the CLAUDE.md rewrite disaster: the author accreted guidelines over time; at some point Claude was allowed to rewrite/compress the file (dedup, contradiction removal); the compressed version was WORSE at keeping Claude working in the author's preferred way; it was reverted (process-evolution.md cites b5c84b2→9bacc8a, −62%, collateral loss of the commit-after-RED rule). Establish: full chronology, what the compression actually changed (diff-level), why it plausibly degraded behavior, what was lost in the revert crossfire, residue today.

EPISODE B — the test-suite reorganization that went wrong: at some point the diagnosis was that the SHAPE of the test suite was steering the model toward writing wrong specs, and a reorganization of the suite was attempted, which failed. Find it: look for spec-tree restructures (directory moves, unit/integration/acceptance/e2e splits, mass renames, "reorganize"/"restructure"/"move" commit subjects), what preceded them (the diagnosis), what followed (reverts, corrections, the e5c7074 fixture→mock swap if related). Establish: what was diagnosed, what change was made, by whom (bot-authored? co-authored?), how it went wrong, what was kept vs reverted, and what of TODAY's spec-tree layout is experiment fallout rather than author intent.

DELIVERABLE: .coordination/claude-experiments.md — chronological executive summary of both episodes (dates, SHAs), era mapping, and a LESSONS section: which patterns visible at HEAD are author-intent vs experiment-fallout, and what each episode teaches for a BDD style guide. No hard-wrapped prose. Return max-15-line executive summary as final text.`, { model: 'opus', effort: 'xhigh', label: 'episodes', phase: 'Investigate' })

phase('Revise')
const revision = await agent(`You are revising /home/user/BookMinder/.coordination/bdd-style-canonical.md IN PLACE. Modify no other file. Full git history available for verification.

THE AUTHOR READ THE CURRENT VERSION AND GAVE THREE CORRECTIONS:

1. THE WHY SECTION IS WRONG. It fused pair programming with verification ("a pair is someone whose claims you can check") — the author calls this totally off base, "merging unrelated concepts". Their ACTUAL motivation, in their words: pair programming is about having a partner to bounce ideas off — discussing what's the next step, how do we define the test, how do we minimize the surface area for the implementation, what are the minimal constraints to express in a spec to get the desired behavior in the next step. THAT is the discipline of pairing in BDD style. It has nothing to do with verifying claims. Rewrite the motivation layer faithfully to this. Separately true (don't delete, just don't fuse): executable specs nail verifiable invariants; long-term evolution vs one-shotting; London school/GOOS; minimal coupling of spec to implementation. Do not tie these into one clever thesis — present motivations as the author holds them, side by side.

2. STRIP ALL META-COMMENTARY about how the document came about — no mention of extractions, judges, syntheses, A/B/C, "this document", provenance notes. The deliverable is a STYLE GUIDE TO BE APPLIED: prescriptive, how-to, each rule with its motivation. Someone (human or agent) should be able to work in this style by following it.

3. SEPARATE AUTHOR INTENT FROM EXPERIMENT FALLOUT. Read .coordination/claude-experiments.md (a just-completed investigation of two episodes where Claude was given autonomy — a CLAUDE.md rewrite disaster and a test-suite reorganization gone wrong). Where the current guide presents a pattern as "the style" that the investigation shows to be fallout of those experiments rather than author intent, fix it: either drop it or explicitly mark it as a known deviation to repair. The guide must describe the style the AUTHOR was going for.

Keep: the high-level→specific structure, evidence SHAs where they teach, the lapse anatomy (as cautionary section), open-wounds list (as repair backlog). Keep mobile formatting (no hard-wrapped prose). Return max-10-line summary of what changed.`, { model: 'fable', effort: 'xhigh', label: 'revise-guide', phase: 'Revise' })

return { episodes, revision }

result.episodes:
`.coordination/claude-experiments.md` written (242 lines; 2 late fact-corrections uncommitted vs `165ccd9`).

**EPISODE A — constitution rewrite (2025-07-22 → 07-31).** `3c27ecc` (bot, unmerged) annotates CLAUDE.md with 31 "PERFORMANCE ISSUE" comments scored purely on reader burden; `b5c84b2` (bot) rewrites 248→91 lines; author improves it in place on the bot's branch (`5292033`, commit-after-RED); merged as PR #12 (`929129e`); reverted wholesale `9bacc8a`/PR #19 eight days later. Diff-level: everything *procedural* was cut (verify-RED step, "no implementation without tests", 19 checklist items, requirements dialogue, session workflow, ATDD-stays-RED, story→describe→it naming), everything *declarative* kept — because the review's criterion measured legibility, not behavioral coverage. `git diff b5c84b2^ 9bacc8a` is empty; `git diff b5c84b2^ HEAD` is +14 (the `xs` block) — zero text residue. Collateral: `5292033` lived *inside* the rewritten hunk, so the single-commit revert erased it cleanly, no conflict. Residue: CLAUDE.md self-contradicts (`<git_workflow>` two commits vs `<tdd_discipline>` verify-RED); the constitution has never described the spec tree (the only sentence that did was the bot's, reverted); AGENTS/GEMINI never synced. Circumstantial: the 7-day compressed window is 57 main commits, **zero** touching `bookminder/` or `specs/`, 51 building `xs` untested → `582820e` repair + 6 characterization-test commits hours after the revert. Correlation exact, causation unprovable from git (scope-exclusion competes).

**EPISODE B — spec-tree reorg (diagnosed 07-08→07-14, executed 07-21, corrected never).** Diagnosis is the author's own: YOLO retrospective's "Test Structure Hijacking" (a flat `cli_spec.py` with unowned `describe_` blocks invited redefinition) plus the `7d3922a` lesson (refactor in place, never grow a parallel suite). Remedy: `be394a0`…`0bf00d1`, one day, human-authored, `Co-Authored-By: Claude` on the first three and stopping exactly at `e5c7074`. **`e5c7074` is the buried casualty**: under "moved all mocked CLI tests… 100% coverage maintained" it deleted `677a251`'s two fixture/subprocess sample tests — including the only guarded one (`assert len(output) > 0`) — and created `describe_bookminder_acceptance` holding mock rewrites with identical `it_` names asserting against their own stubs. `pytest --spec` output unchanged; sample filtering has had no falsifiable end-to-end spec since 2025-07-21. `9781be1` invented the `_integration` suffixes purely to dodge a name collision. PR #18 (`447dc8c`…`55f2b4e`, all claude[bot], unmerged) failed because it could not hold two baselines apart — deleted `specs/e2e/` it had promised to preserve, restored it 99 minutes later, abandoned at +176/−9,086. `docs/SPECS_REVIEW.md` (`b84f56e`, 2025-10, unmerged) nails it — "the failure wasn't execution, it was conception"; "taxonomy is discovered, not imposed" — but itself misses the falsifiability loss.

**LESSONS.** Author-intent at HEAD: describe/it + `--spec` as living docs, story→describe→it naming, outside-in ATDD, commit after RED/GREEN/REFACTOR, coordination-not-output mockist boundaries (`552a9a3`), ONE subprocess test, real fixtures, docstrings only on pending specs. Fallout, not style: the four-layer tree and its `__init__.py` contracts (never adopted by the constitution), `describe_bookminder_acceptance`, `describe_bookminder_integration`-in-`e2e/`, `_integration` suffixes, duplicate describes, dead `TEST_HOME`, unit tests of private helpers, `cli.SUPPORTED_FILTERS` patch target (mutated by `fa0bc72` to make RED pass), TODO/story status disagreement. Transferable rules: never let an agent rewrite a rules file wholesale (it fuses history into one un-revertable hunk); a rule's friction is often its function; **"all tests pass, coverage unchanged" cannot validate a change to the tests** — review spec commits by diff, and treat "pure move" as a claim to verify; same `it_` name + weaker assertion is the most dangerous edit in a BDD suite; the patch target is part of the specification; both episodes are one failure — optimizing a meta-artifact against a proxy (readability, tidiness) at the cost of falsifiability, checked by the very apparatus being changed.
result.revision:
Revision complete at /home/user/BookMinder/.coordination/bdd-style-canonical.md. Summary of changes:

1. §1 rewritten: pairing now presented as thinking partnership (bounce ideas — next step, test definition, minimal implementation surface, minimal spec constraints), with the verification/pair fusion removed; other motivations (verifiable invariants, long-term evolution, GOOS/minimal coupling, code-as-liability) kept side by side as separate motivations, no organizing thesis.
2. All provenance meta stripped: synthesis/extraction/judge intro deleted, "one extraction proposed", "no extraction caught", "verified this session" removed; reframed as a prescriptive guide ("The BookMinder BDD Style Guide") with SHAs as teaching citations.
3. §2.2 no longer presents the four-layer directory taxonomy as house style — mock rules now defined per test *kind* (pure-logic/collaborator/coordination/one-subprocess), with the taxonomy explicitly marked as an abandoned one-day experiment (`be394a0`…`0bf00d1`, post-mortem `b84f56e`) pending repair; §2.3 bullets renamed off directory names.
4. Docstring rule corrected to author intent (pending skipped specs only); layer `__init__.py` contracts removed as an exception (marked as ratification fallout); given-docstring `30c2fe5` moved to §6 Unsettled.
5. Commit-after-RED (`5292033`) restored as a first-class sequence rule in §2.6; §3 cadence adjusted to match.
6. New §2.7: suite and constitution are production artifacts — diff-review spec commits, same-`it_`-weaker-assertion danger, patch-target-is-spec, no wholesale rules-file rewrites, friction-is-function.
7. §4 lapse anatomy kept (a–h intact) plus a compact "meta-artifact lapses" paragraph covering both autonomy episodes.
8. §5 backlog extended and re-verified against the working tree: taxonomy decision, CLAUDE.md self-contradiction/AGENTS-GEMINI drift, status-ledger conflict, duplicate `it_` names (`:154`/`:200`), README:98 rot; line refs corrected (`cli.py:10`).
